tool_input.prompt:
I need to map this codebase's architecture to Java Spring Boot equivalents. Explore and report back the CONCRETE structure of the TypeScript backend so I can write accurate parallels.

Read these files and report their key contents/patterns (don't dump whole files, summarize the shapes):

1. `docs/BACKEND.md` — report the major sections: bounded context folder structure, dependency direction, event architecture (UnitOfWork/Outbox/Mediators), DI & registries, schema strategy, authorization, SDK pipeline. Give me concrete class/interface names.

2. Look at ONE real bounded context under `packages/api/typescript/src/` — pick a representative one (e.g. a context folder with entities, use-cases, controllers, repositories). List the actual folder structure (tree) and pick 1 example of each citizen (entity, use case, controller, repository, registry) and show me its skeleton — class signature, decorators (tsyringe @injectable etc), how DI works, how a controller is wired, how a use case declares InputSchema/OutputSchema.

3. The registry.ts wiring file of that context — show how BoundedContext.create({...}) works with INSTANCE_REGISTRY mock/integration/real keys.

4. How HTTP routing/controllers register (the framework — is it a custom router? Hono? show the controller base class).

5. How tsyringe DI container is structured (the equivalent of Spring's ApplicationContext).

Report concrete names: base classes, decorators, interfaces. I want enough to draw exact parallels to Spring Boot (@RestController, @Service, @Repository, @Entity, ApplicationContext, @Transactional, ApplicationEventPublisher, etc).

file.content:
# Backend Architecture

> Full architectural reference for the TypeScript `api` and Go `channel` backends.
> The **why** behind the patterns. For **how** to implement each artifact, load the matching `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.

The project is **DDD + Clean Architecture + CQRS + Event-Driven**. Every rule below exists to keep bounded contexts independent so the system can evolve without rewrites.

---

## Bounded Contexts

### TypeScript (`packages/api`)

`agent`, `appointment`, `auth`, `clinic`, `collaborator`, `doctor`, `patient`, `service`, `unit`, `ui`, `external`, `shared`.

Each context owns the same folder shape:

```
src/<context>/
├── controllers/     # HTTP endpoints + Zod schemas
├── entities/        # Aggregate roots + entities (rich behavior)
├── enums/           # Closed vocabularies (use TS `enum` + pgEnum)
├── errors/          # Domain + application errors with HTTP mapping
├── events/          # Domain events raised by entities
├── handlers/
│   ├── internal.ts  # Reacts to events from THIS context (write-side side-effects)
│   └── external.ts  # Reacts to integration events from OTHER contexts/services
├── middlewares/
├── objects/         # Value objects (immutable, self-validating)
├── projections/
│   ├── <Name>.ts                          # Projection record + applyX methods (read-side)
│   ├── <Name>ProjectionRepository.ts      # Interface + Drizzle impl + Mock (atomic ops)
│   └── projectors/
│       └── <Name>Projector.ts             # One per projection — outbox-dispatched
├── repositories/    # Interface + Drizzle implementation + Mock (write-side aggregates)
├── services/        # Domain/application services
├── usecases/        # Application commands (one per business operation)
├── registry.ts      # Per-context DI bindings (mock / integration / real)
└── index.ts         # BoundedContext.create({...}) — wires the context
```

Two contexts are special:
- **`ui`** — owns **query use cases** (BFF reads with direct Drizzle access). It does not own aggregates.
- **`shared`** — base classes, mediators, outbox infrastructure, integration-event payloads, DI composition.

### Go (`packages/channel`)

Mirrors the same shape (`controllers`, `entities`, `usecases`, `services`, `repositories`, `events`, `handlers`) and adds a **`projections/`** layer that materializes Kafka payloads into `channel_*` tables (read by the TS BFF via Drizzle).

---

## First-Class Citizens

These are the building blocks the codebase is composed of. Each has a corresponding `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` that is the authoritative playbook.

| Citizen | Lives in | Role | Relates to |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BoundedContext** | `<ctx>/index.ts` | Wires controllers, handlers, middlewares; owns the context's DI container | Aggregates everything below |
| **Entity / AggregateRoot** | `<ctx>/entities/` | Identity + business behavior + invariants; raises domain events | Composed of value objects + enums; persisted by repository |
| **Value Object** | `<ctx>/objects/` | Immutable, self-validating concept without identity (CPF, Money, Email) | Embedded in entities |
| **Enum** | `<ctx>/enums/` | Closed vocabulary (statuses, types) — paired with `pgEnum` | Used by entities + schemas |
| **Domain Error / Application Error** | `<ctx>/errors/` | Typed errors with code + HTTP status + i18n key | Thrown by entities (domain) and use cases (application) |
| **Schema** | `<ctx>/controllers/.../schemas` | Zod input/output for one controller | Compiled into SDK Zod schemas |
| **Controller** | `<ctx>/controllers/` | HTTP boundary; validates with schemas; delegates to a use case | Calls use cases; never touches repositories |
| **Use Case (command)** | `<ctx>/usecases/` | Orchestrates aggregates inside a `UnitOfWork`; persists via repositories; saves domain events through `DomainEventRepository` | Called by controller; touches entities + repositories |
| **Query Use Case** | `ui/usecases/` | Read-only DTOs assembled with direct Drizzle queries (BFF) | Bypasses aggregate rehydration on purpose |
| **Repository** | `<ctx>/repositories/` | Interface + `DrizzleXRepository` + `MockXRepository`; loads/saves aggregates | Receives entity; returns entity; supports `tx` |
| **Service** | `<ctx>/services/` | Logic that doesn't fit in an entity or spans aggregates / external APIs | Composed by use cases |
| **Domain Event** | `<ctx>/events/` | Past-tense fact within this context; raised by entity behavior | Picked up by `internalHandlers`; never crosses service boundary |
| **Integration Event** | `shared/events/` (TS and Go) | Cross-context / cross-service contract published to Kafka | Translated **only** by a domain handler |
| **Handler (internal)** | `<ctx>/handlers/internal.ts` | Reacts to **this** context's domain events with write-side side-effects; may publish integration events | Listens via `InternalMediator` |
| **Handler (external)** | `<ctx>/handlers/external.ts` | Reacts to integration events from other contexts/services | Listens via `ExternalMediator` |
| **Projection** | `<ctx>/projections/<Name>.ts` | Free record class — no base class. `constructor(public props: <Name>ProjectionProps)`. Zod schema defines the shape. Exports `type <Name>ProjectionEvent` (union of events that affect it). Method-overloaded `static create(event)` (one signature per creating event) and `applyEvent(event)` (one signature per mutating event); each has a single implementation with `switch (event.name)`. **No invariants** | Written by `Projector`; read by query use cases / BFF |
| **ProjectionRepository** | `<ctx>/projections/<Name>ProjectionRepository.ts` | Three canonical methods: `findByKey`, `save`, `insertIfNew` — enough for the `find → applyEvent → save` flow. Atomic ops (`incrementX`, `markDeliveredMany`, `setIfGreater*`) are edge-case additions for hot rows, bulk ops, monotonic constraints, conditional updates, or cache-mirror upserts | No shared base — each repo declares its own surface |
| **Projector** | `<ctx>/projections/projectors/<Name>Projector.ts` | Read-side counterpart of EventHandler. One per Projection. Generic from the projection (`extends Projector<MessageProjectionEvent>`). `handle(event, tx?)` uses **plain `switch (event.name)`** with `default: never` exhaustiveness. **Canonical: `find → applyEvent → save`.** Async via outbox by default; inline opt-in for read-after-write within a UoW | Only knows its `ProjectionRepository` |
| **Middleware** | `<ctx>/middlewares/` | HTTP cross-cutting (auth, tenancy, logging) | Wired in `BoundedContext.create` |
| **Registry** | `<ctx>/registry.ts` | DI bindings keyed by env (`mock` / `integration` / `real`) | Aggregated by `shared/registry.ts` into `ALL_REGISTRIES` |
| **UnitOfWork** | `shared/services` (`UnitOfWorkFactory`) | Transaction boundary across multiple repositories | Used inside command use cases |
| **InternalMediator** | `shared/services` | In-process dispatch (EventEmitter2) of domain events | Triggered by `OutboxDispatcher` |
| **ExternalMediator** | `shared/services` | Cross-service publishing (Redis/Kafka prod, EventEmitter2 integration, Mock in tests) | Used **only by domain handlers** |
| **OutboxDispatcher** | `shared/services` | Polls `outbox`, dispatches to `InternalMediator`, marks processed | `DrizzleOutboxDispatcher` in integration/real |
| **DomainEventRepository** | `shared/repositories` | Persists events to `events` (audit) + `outbox` (dispatch) in one tx | Called by use cases / handlers |

---

## Dependency Direction (the only diagram that matters)

```
            ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │                     Controller                         │  HTTP boundary
            └────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                 │ calls
            ┌────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────┐
            │            Use Case  (command)        Query Use Case   │  Application
            └────┬────────────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────┘
                 │ uses               │ persists         │ reads (Drizzle)
                 │                    │                  │
            ┌────▼──────┐    ┌────────▼────────┐    ┌────▼────────────┐
            │  Entity   │    │   Repository    │    │  Projection     │
            │  + VOs    │◄───┤  (write side —  │    │  table          │◄─ written by
            │  + Events │    │   aggregates)   │    │  (read model)   │     Projector
            └────┬──────┘    └─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
                 │ raises
            ┌────▼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │  Domain Event  →  events + outbox tables             │
            └────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │ poll
            ┌────▼─────────────┐    InternalMediator (fan-out)
            │ OutboxDispatcher ├──┬─►──────────────────┐
            └──────────────────┘  │                    │
                                  ▼                    ▼
                       ┌──────────────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐
                       │ Internal Handler │  │ Projector         │
                       │ (write-side fx)  │  │ (read-side fx)    │
                       └─────────┬────────┘  └─────────┬─────────┘
                                 │ may publish         │ atomic ops
                       ┌─────────▼────────┐  ┌─────────▼─────────┐
                       │ Integration      │  │ Projection-       │
                       │ Event            │  │ Repository        │
                       │ (ExternalMediator│  │ (insertIfNew,     │
                       │  → Kafka)        │  │  incrementX, …)   │
                       └─────────┬────────┘  └───────────────────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                       ┌──────────────────┐
                       │ External Handler │  another context /
                       │ (consumer)       │  another service
                       └──────────────────┘
```

**Hard rules:**

- Controllers never touch repositories. They call use cases.
- Entities and value objects know **nothing** about HTTP, persistence, or DI.
- Cross-context calls happen via repository reads (synchronous, intra-process) or integration events (async, cross-service). Direct imports of another context's entities or domain events are forbidden.
- The SDK HTTP client is for the frontend — never use it from inside `api`.
- Database schema is **derived from** the validated entity model — never the other way around.
- Projection tables are written **only** by Projectors (or by ACL/sync code via the same `ProjectionRepository`, for archetypes A and B1). Use cases never touch them.
- Projectors never touch aggregates, never publish integration events, never call use cases. Their only dependency is a `ProjectionRepository`.

---

## Event Architecture

Events are the backbone of cross-aggregate and cross-service communication. There are **three event layers** and only one legitimate translation point between them.

### The three layers

| Layer | Type | Where | Scope | Transport |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Domain Event** | `BaseDomainEvent` (TS) / `DomainEvent` (Go) | `<ctx>/events/` | Inside one bounded context | `events` + `outbox` tables → `InternalMediator` (in-process) |
| **Gateway Event** (Go only) | `DomainEvent` | `channel/events/gateway_*` | Raw WhatsApp platform events | Same outbox pattern as domain events |
| **Integration Event** | `BaseIntegrationEvent` (TS) / `IntegrationEvent` (Go) | `shared/events/` | Cross-context / cross-service contract | `ExternalMediator` → Kafka (Go ↔ TS) or in-process emitter (intra-service) |

### The canonical flow

```
Entity behavior method
    └─► entity.addDomainEvent(…)                       (raise)

Use case  (inside UnitOfWork)
    ├─► repository.save(entity, tx)
    └─► domainEventRepository.save(event, tx)          (write events + outbox in same tx)

OutboxDispatcher                                       (background)
    ├─► poll outbox  (SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
    ├─► internalMediator.dispatch(event)               (fan-out to all subscribers)
    └─► mark processed / increment attempts / dead-letter

InternalMediator (fan-out)
    │
    ├─► Internal Handler          (per-context, registered in handlers/internal.ts)
    │     ├─► may update other aggregates of THIS context (via their use cases)
    │     └─► may externalMediator.publish(integrationEvent)  ← THE ONLY translation point
    │
    └─► Projector                 (read-side, registered in projections/projectors/)
          ├─► chooses Path A (find → projection.applyX → save)
          └─► or Path B (repo atomic op: insertIfNew / incrementX / setIfGreater)

Kafka  (Go ↔ TS)
    └─► consumer in target service triggers an external handler / use case
```

Internal handlers and projectors are **siblings** on the same fan-out — both subscribed via `InternalMediator`, both dispatched by the same outbox row. The difference is intent: handlers produce write-side effects (call use cases, publish integration events); projectors update read-models (atomic ops on projection tables). They share a delivery lifecycle but never depend on each other.

### Who is allowed to do what

| Action | Allowed in | Forbidden in |
|---|---|---|
| Raise a domain event | Entity behavior methods | Use cases, services, controllers, handlers, projectors |
| Save a domain event | Use cases, handlers (always through `domainEventRepository.save`) | Entities, controllers, projectors |
| Dispatch a domain event | `OutboxDispatcher` only | Everywhere else |
| Handle a domain event (write-side) | `handlers/internal.ts` of the same context | Other contexts (use integration events) |
| Handle a domain event (read-side) | `projections/projectors/<Name>Projector.ts` (own or other contexts' events) | Anywhere it would mutate aggregates |
| Publish an integration event | `handlers/internal.ts` of the originating context | Use cases, entities, services, controllers, external handlers, projectors |
| Consume an integration event | `handlers/external.ts` (TS) or Kafka consumer (Go); also `projectors/` if the consumer is read-side | Anywhere it would couple to another context's domain types |
| Write to a projection table | `projectors/` via `ProjectionRepository` (read-side) **or** ACL/sync code via the same repo (archetypes A / B1) | Use cases, handlers, controllers |

**Why these rules:** the outbox guarantees a domain event is persisted atomically with the state change, so no in-flight crash can drop it. The "only handlers translate" rule means integration contracts can only change when a handler changes — use cases never become coupled to Kafka.

### Cross-context vs cross-service

- **Same process (intra-service)** — another context can listen to a domain event directly via `InternalMediator` if both are wired into the same container. Or it can listen to an integration event for stronger isolation. Channel's `messaging` and `chat` contexts listen to `channel.gateway_*` domain events this way.
- **Different services (Go ↔ TS)** — integration events via Kafka are the **only** legal channel.

Reaction rule for new cross-context behavior: **never** import another context's entity or domain event. Listen to its integration event in `handlers/external.ts`.

### Persistence model

Both services share the same outbox schema:

```sql
-- Permanent audit log (append-only)
events  (id, name, entity_id, owner_id, payload jsonb, time, updated_at, version)

-- Transient dispatch queue (poll → dispatch → delete/mark)
outbox  (id, name, owner_id, payload jsonb, time, created_at, updated_at,
         version, processed_at, attempts)
```

Integration event payload shapes live in `shared/events/` of each service and can be reused by domain event payloads to avoid duplication.

### Domain event delivery is awaited; integration event publishing is fire-and-forget

- `InternalMediator.dispatch()` awaits handler execution and propagates errors (so the outbox row stays unprocessed and retries).
- `ExternalMediator.publish()` does not wait for downstream — Kafka backpressure and durability are infrastructure concerns, not the publisher's.

### End-to-end walk-through

A single business operation traverses every layer of the system. The example below traces `ConfirmAppointment` from the controller down to a WhatsApp notification, showing exactly which citizen is in control at each step and what each one is allowed to touch.

```
1. CONTROLLER                            packages/api/src/appointment/controllers/
   ConfirmAppointmentController.execute(request)
     ├─► validates request via InputSchema (Zod)
     └─► calls ConfirmAppointment use case

2. USE CASE (inside UnitOfWork)          packages/api/src/appointment/usecases/
   ConfirmAppointment.execute({ appointmentId, memberId })
     │
     ├─► uow = unitOfWorkFactory.create()
     └─► uow.transaction(async tx => {
           │
           ├─► appointment = await appointmentRepository.findById(id, tx)
           │     │   loads aggregate from `appointments` table
           │     └─► returns rehydrated entities.Appointment
           │
           ├─► appointment.confirm()                         ◄── ENTITY METHOD
           │     │   validates invariant: not cancelled, not already confirmed
           │     │   mutates state: status = CONFIRMED
           │     └─► entity.addDomainEvent(AppointmentConfirmed)
           │
           ├─► await appointmentRepository.save(appointment, tx)
           │     │   UPDATE on `appointments`
           │     └─► (does NOT persist events — that's the next step)
           │
           └─► await domainEventRepository.save(pullEvents(appointment), tx)
                 │   INSERT into `events` (audit log, permanent)
                 └─► INSERT into `outbox`  (dispatch queue, transient)
   })  ←─ COMMIT. State change + event persistence are atomic.

3. OUTBOX DISPATCHER (background, polls every N ms)
   OutboxDispatcher.poll()
     │
     ├─► SELECT FROM outbox WHERE processed_at IS NULL
     │     FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT n
     │     (concurrent dispatchers don't fight over the same rows)
     │
     ├─► for each row:
     │     await internalMediator.dispatch(event)   ◄── FAN-OUT TO ALL SUBSCRIBERS
     │
     └─► UPDATE outbox SET processed_at = now()
         (or increment attempts on failure; retry until dead-lettered)

4. INTERNAL MEDIATOR (in-process fan-out)
   internalMediator.emit('appointment.appointment_confirmed', event)
     │
     ├─► subscriber #1: AppointmentConfirmedInternalHandler  (handlers/internal.ts)
     │     │
     │     ├─► may load other appointment aggregates (e.g. cancel the patient's
     │     │   conflicting tentative appointment via use case)
     │     │
     │     └─► await externalMediator.publish(                  ◄── THE ONLY
     │           new AppointmentConfirmedIntegrationEvent({          PLACE THIS
     │             appointmentId, patientId, doctorId,              IS ALLOWED
     │             clinicId, confirmedAt,
     │           })
     │         )
     │
     └─► subscriber #2: PatientProjector                     (projections/projectors/)
           │
           │  This projection lives in the `patient` context but listens to events
           │  from `appointment` — cross-aggregate, but legal because both are
           │  registered on the same InternalMediator (same process).
           │
           └─► await patientProjectionRepo.setIfGreaterNextAppointment(
                 patientId, confirmedAt
               )                                              ◄── PATH B: atomic op,
                                                                  no find, no race.

5. EXTERNAL MEDIATOR (in process for integration mode; Kafka for real)
   externalMediator.publish(integrationEvent)
     │
     ├─► production: writes to Redis stream / Kafka topic `bk-dash.shared.events`
     ├─► integration tests: in-process EventEmitter2 (synchronous)
     └─► flow tests: MockExternalMediator captures, doesn't publish

6. CROSS-SERVICE CONSUMER (Go channel service, separate process)
   Kafka consumer picks up `shared.appointment_confirmed`
     │
     └─► AppointmentConfirmedExternalHandler.handle(event)   (Go: handlers/external.ts)
           │
           ├─► resolves the patient's WhatsApp remote
           ├─► calls SendWhatsAppMessage use case (Go-side)
           │     │
           │     ├─► loads Channel aggregate, calls channel.sendMessage(...)
           │     ├─► persists Message + domain event MessageSent
           │     └─► (same outbox pattern; this is a new transaction in the Go service)
           │
           └─► (eventually) the channel service's outbox dispatches MessageSent
                 │
                 └─► MessageProjector inserts a row in `channel_messages`
                       via repo.insertIfNew(...)             ◄── PATH B
                 └─► RemoteProjector bumps remote.lastMessageAt
                       via repo.setIfGreaterLastMessageAt(...)
```

The key idea: **no citizen knows about the next one directly.** The controller doesn't know there's a handler; the use case doesn't know there are projectors; the internal handler doesn't know which contexts consume the integration event. The wiring lives in `BoundedContext.create` (registrations) and in the `InternalMediator` / Kafka topology. Adding a third subscriber to `AppointmentConfirmed` — say, an `AnalyticsProjector` that bumps a `daily_confirmed_count` — means writing one new Projector file and registering it. No other file changes.

### Why the fan-out has two flavours (handler vs projector)

| Concern | Internal Handler | Projector |
|---|---|---|
| Where it lives | `<ctx>/handlers/internal.ts` | `<ctx>/projections/projectors/<Name>Projector.ts` |
| What it writes | Aggregates (via use cases) **or** integration events | Projection tables only |
| What it depends on | Use cases, `ExternalMediator`, other repositories | One `ProjectionRepository` |
| Allowed to publish integration events | **Yes** — the only place | **No** |
| Allowed to call use cases | **Yes** | **No** |
| Failure semantics | Outbox row stays unprocessed; retried | Same — outbox-aware retries |
| Test surface | TestBed integration mode; assert on aggregate state + emitted integration events | TestBed integration mode; assert on projection row state |

If a piece of behaviour wants to do both (e.g. update an aggregate **and** advance a denormalised counter), it splits in two: a handler for the aggregate path, a projector for the counter path. Each one stays narrow.

---

## Read-Model Architecture (structural)

CQRS in this project is **logical**, not physical — the same Postgres database holds both write-side aggregates and read-side projections. The split is at the type-system level: separate types, separate repositories, separate responsibilities.

This section documents the **architectural structure** only. For modelling guidance — when to introduce a projection, which archetype to use, how denormalized to go, Path A vs Path B — load `.claude/skills/projection/SKILL.md`. The skill carries the 4-archetype decision framework, the denormalization spectrum, the Path A/B rules, and the smell tests.

### Aggregate vs Projection — two types, two interfaces

For any concept with identity + state, you may have **both** of these:

| | Aggregate | Projection |
|---|---|---|
| File | `<ctx>/entities/X.ts` | `<ctx>/projections/X.ts` |
| Definition style | Zod schema → `z.infer<>` → class extending `BaseEntity<Props>` (or `AggregateRoot<Props>`) + `.create()` factory that validates | **Free record** — plain class with `constructor(public props: Props)`. **No base class.** Flat Zod schema; no `.transform()`; no validation on construction. |
| Purpose | Enforce invariants, raise domain events on state changes | Materialise read-shape for a specific UI/query need |
| Has methods? | Yes — `.create(input)` factory + behaviour methods that validate + mutate + `addDomainEvent` | Yes — overloaded `static create(event)` (one signature per creating event) + overloaded instance `applyEvent(event)` (one signature per mutating event). Each is a single implementation that switches on `event.name`. No raised events |
| Has invariants? | **Yes** — domain rules live here | **No** — rules already enforced upstream |
| Has identity? | Yes (aggregate root id) | Yes (natural key — may include composite columns) |
| Written by | `<ctx>/repositories/XRepository.save(entity)` inside a use case's `UnitOfWork` | `<ctx>/projections/projectors/*` — async via outbox by default; inline within a use case's `UoW` allowed as opt-in |
| Read by | Use cases only (write-side) | Query use cases / BFF (read-side) |

A field belongs on the aggregate **only if a business rule reads it**. Otherwise it's projection-only. Counters, denormalised joins, last-event timestamps, derived ranks, cached external fields — those go on the projection.

### Projector wiring

Projectors are registered in `BoundedContext.create({ projectors })` alongside `internalHandlers` and `externalHandlers`. The `OutboxDispatcher` invokes them through `InternalMediator` — one outbox row triggers all matching subscribers (handlers + projectors) for that event name.

A Projector may live in context **X** but subscribe to events from context **Y** (cross-aggregate). This is fine — the two contexts share the same process and `InternalMediator`. The only rule: the Projector imports the event **class** from `Y`, not `Y`'s entities or repositories.

The Projector class's signature lives in the projector skill. Briefly: it extends `Projector<E>` for some event union `E` (imported from its Projection), declares `readonly events: readonly string[]`, and implements `handle(event, tx?)` with a plain `switch (event.name)` plus a `default: never` for exhaustiveness. Canonical mutation flow is `find → applyEvent → save`. Atomic ops on the repo are edge cases — used when a canonical `find → applyEvent → save` would fail (hot rows, bulk operations, monotonic constraints, conditional updates, cache-mirror upserts). Full shape, rules, and examples live in `.claude/skills/projector/SKILL.md`.

**Synchronous inline option:** a use case MAY invoke a projector synchronously inside its own `UnitOfWork` (`projector.handle(event, tx)`) for read-after-write consistency. This couples the use case to the projector by design — used only when the same request must see the projection update. Default remains async outbox.

**Cross-aggregate cross-context** read shapes (spanning multiple bounded contexts) live in the `ui` (BFF) context — `ui/projections/<Name>.ts` + `ui/projections/projectors/<Name>Projector.ts`. The BFF is the architectural place where cross-context coupling is allowed. Domain contexts only host projections for their own aggregates.

### Channel projection ownership (Go-specific)

The Go `channel` service uses the same architecture but predates the codified primitives. Its `channel_*` tables are owned by Go (Go writes via its projectors; TS reads via Drizzle mirror schemas). The schema-drift integration test in `packages/api/src/ui/usecases/channel/channel-schema-drift.test.ts` catches Go-side migrations that haven't been mirrored to the TS Drizzle schema.

> Full applied case for channel: `.specs/2026-04-17-aggregate-projection-architecture.md`.

---

## Schema Strategy

Validation happens at two edges:

1. **Controller schemas** — expressive (regex, refine, format checks, cross-field rules). Face external input.
2. **Entity / Value Object `.create()`** — domain invariants (business rules). Trusted by use cases.

Use case schemas in the middle are **simple primitives** because they trust the controller validated format and the entity will validate domain rules.

```typescript
// Controller — expressive
const InputSchema = z.object({
  body: z.object({
    email: z.email(),
    password: z.string().min(8).regex(/^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)/),
    document: z.string(),
  }),
}).refine(d => isValidCPF(d.body.document), { path: ['document'], message: 'INVALID_CPF' })

// Use case — primitive
export const CreateAccountInputSchema = z.object({
  email: z.string(),
  password: z.string(),
  document: z.string(),
})
```

### Other schema rules

- **Enums in Zod**: `z.enum(OrderStatus)` — never `z.union([z.literal('A'), ...])`.
- **Query params are strings**: use `z.stringToNumber()`, `z.stringToBoolean()`, `z.stringToDate()`, `z.stringToArray()`.
- **Schema builders**: `z.paginatedQuery({...})`, `z.paginatedResponse({...})`, `z.domainEvent({...})`, `z.integrationEvent({...})`.
- **Primitive in, Value Object inside** — `.create()` accepts primitives and constructs VOs internally; never accept VOs as parameters.
- **Centralized enum registration**: all enums are spread into `packages/api/src/shared/index.ts` so OpenAPI names them by context (`AppointmentStatus`, not `Status`). Never call `openapi.registerEnums()` inside a context — integration events from other contexts would resolve to fallback names.

---

## Cross-Context Communication (intra-process)

Inside `api`, synchronous cross-context business validation uses **repository reads directly**:

```typescript
// ✅ Read for validation
const customer = await this.customerRepository.findById(new Id(customerId), tx)
if (!customer) throw new BaseError<ApplicationErrors>('CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND')

// ❌ Pass-through use case just to check existence
// ❌ Importing another context's controller or entity
// ❌ Calling the SDK HTTP client from inside api
```

When to use which:

| Scenario | Approach |
|---|---|
| Validate entity exists in another context | Repository read (`findById`, `findBy*`) |
| Need synchronous data for a business rule | Repository read |
| Modify another context's state | Integration Event + external handler |
| Need transactional atomicity across contexts | Re-evaluate boundaries — usually a sign of accidental coupling |

---

## Error Handling

| Type | When | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **DomainErrors** | Business invariants | `INSUFFICIENT_STOCK`, `INVALID_EMAIL` |
| **ApplicationErrors** | Application-level conditions | `PATIENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ALREADY_EXISTS` |
| **InterfaceErrors** | Auth / transport-level | `UNAUTHORIZED`, `SESSION_EXPIRED` |

Backend flow:
1. Declare error codes in `<ctx>/errors/index.ts` (separated by type — `DomainErrors`, `ApplicationErrors`, `InterfaceErrors`).
2. Register them in `GlobalErrorMapper` with the right HTTP status. Status carries semantic meaning the frontend reads:
   - `UNAUTHORIZED (401)` — no/invalid session
   - `FORBIDDEN (403)` — authenticated but not allowed in this flow (e.g. `ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED`)
   - `NOT_FOUND (404)` — resource doesn't exist for this user
   - `CONFLICT (409)` — state conflict (e.g. `ALREADY_EXISTS`)
3. Throw via `BaseError<ErrorType>('ERROR_CODE')` from entities (`DomainError`), use cases / handlers / middlewares (`ApplicationError`, `InterfaceError`).
4. Run `bun sdk` so the code lands in `ApiErrorsEnum` and the frontend can match on it.

### The error name IS the contract

Every error code that crosses the wire is a contract between backend and frontend. **The frontend can react with custom routing or UI based on the code.** This is most useful for middlewares that enforce flow gates — when a guard fails, the typed code becomes a redirect instruction on the frontend.

### Backend → Frontend error flow (end-to-end)

```
Backend (use case / handler / middleware)
    └─► throw new BaseError<ApplicationErrors>('ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED')

GlobalErrorMapper
    └─► ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED → 403 FORBIDDEN
        Response body: { code: 'ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED', message: '...' }

SDK (Kubb-generated)
    └─► Throws the typed error up to React Query

Frontend — main.tsx
    ├─► QueryCache.onError  → handleApiError(error)
    └─► MutationCache.onError → handleApiError(error)

Frontend — lib/errors.ts
    ├─► extractErrorCode(error) → 'ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED'
    ├─► customErrorHandlers[code] ?? defaultErrorHandler
    └─► Custom handler runs: router.navigate({ to: '/onboarding' })
        (default would be: toast.error(translatedMessage))
```

A middleware that throws `ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED` does NOT need any per-component handling on the frontend — the global `customErrorHandlers` dispatcher routes every query/mutation that hits this code to `/onboarding`.

For the full middleware contract (singleton, ctx parsing, error registration) see `.claude/skills/middleware/SKILL.md`. The frontend half of this flow is documented in `docs/FRONTEND.md` → "API Error Handling".

---

## Authorization & Session Context

Authentication uses a **layered middleware chain** built on the `Middleware` primitive (see `.claude/skills/middleware/SKILL.md`):

```
BetterAuth session
  → AuthAccountMiddleware (validates session → ctx.user, ctx.session)
    → AuthActorMiddleware (validates ctx.session.actorType + actorId → ctx.actor)
      → (optional) OnboardingMiddleware (checks user completed onboarding)
        → Controller.execute()
```

**Key principle:** `ctx` is the single carrier for both session and actor data. `AuthAccountMiddleware` attaches `ctx.user` + `ctx.session` (incl. `actorType`, `actorId`, `ownerId` from the DB session). `AuthActorMiddleware` validates the actor exists for the given type and attaches `ctx.actor`.

### Middleware responsibilities

| Middleware | Lives in | Purpose | Throws on failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AuthAccountMiddleware` | `auth/middlewares/` | BetterAuth session validation; attaches `ctx.user` + `ctx.session` | `UNAUTHORIZED` |
| `AuthActorMiddleware` | `auth/middlewares/` | Validates `actorType` (DOCTOR/COLLABORATOR) + `actorId` against the corresponding repo; attaches `ctx.actor` | `UNAUTHORIZED` |
| `OnboardingMiddleware` | `ui/middlewares/` | User completed onboarding | `ONBOARDING_NOT_COMPLETED` (frontend redirects — see Error Handling above) |

### Context-level defaults

Each bounded context declares default middlewares in `middlewares/index.ts` (default export — never `import * as`):

| Context | Default Middlewares |
|---|---|
| `agent`, `appointment`, `clinic`, `collaborator`, `doctor`, `patient`, `service`, `unit` | `[AuthAccountMiddleware, AuthActorMiddleware]` |
| `ui` | `[AuthAccountMiddleware, OnboardingMiddleware]` |
| `auth`, `external` | (custom — typically only `AuthAccountMiddleware` or none) |

Per-controller overrides use `override middlewares` to **add** and `override skipMiddlewares` to **remove**. Never duplicate a default — it's redundant.

### What lives in `ctx`

| Field | Source | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| `ctx.user` (`id`, `name`, `image`) | BetterAuth session | `AuthAccountMiddleware` |
| `ctx.session` (`actorType`, `actorId`, `ownerId`, …) | BetterAuth session + DB session refresh | `AuthAccountMiddleware` |
| `ctx.actor` (`{ id, type }`) | Verified against `doctor` / `collaborator` repo | `AuthActorMiddleware` |

### Extending session data

- **New session/user field** — declare in BetterAuth `additionalFields`, update `SessionSchema` in `ExtraTypes.ts`, migrate the column.
- **New actor type or guard** — write a new `<Name>Middleware` (see `.claude/skills/middleware/SKILL.md`), declare its error code in `<ctx>/errors/index.ts`, map status in `GlobalErrorMapper`, register a frontend custom handler if you want routing-by-error.
- **Consuming `ctx.user`** — declare `ctx: z.object({ user: z.object({ id: z.string() }) })` in InputSchema; `AuthAccountMiddleware` provides it.

BetterAuth `before` / `after` hooks on auth routes (`/sign-in`, `/sign-up`) are the place to validate custom fields or set session-derived cookies.

---

## Dependency Injection & Registries

The container is **tsyringe-neo**. Every binding is keyed by environment.

```
ALL_REGISTRIES = SHARED_REGISTRY ⊕ agent ⊕ appointment ⊕ auth ⊕ clinic
                ⊕ collaborator ⊕ doctor ⊕ patient ⊕ service ⊕ unit ⊕ ui
```

Each context exports its own bindings in `<ctx>/registry.ts`; `shared/registry.ts` composes them into `ALL_REGISTRIES.mock`, `ALL_REGISTRIES.integration`, `ALL_REGISTRIES.real`.

Environment intent:

| Env | Driver | Mediators | Outbox | DomainEventRepo | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **mock** | `MockUnitOfWorkFactory` | both `EventEmitter2` / `Mock` | `MockOutboxDispatcher` | `OutboxAwareMockDomainEventRepository` | flow tests only |
| **integration** | `PGliteDriver` | both `EventEmitter2` | `DrizzleOutboxDispatcher` | `DrizzleDomainEventRepository` | repository / use case / handler tests |
| **real** | `NodePgDriver` | `EventEmitter2` + `RedisExternalMediator` | `DrizzleOutboxDispatcher` | `DrizzleDomainEventRepository` | production |

Every new context **must**:
1. Create `<ctx>/registry.ts` exporting `INSTANCE_REGISTRY` with all three keys.
2. Be imported and spread into `shared/registry.ts`.
3. Provide both a mock and a concrete binding for each context-scoped repository / service.

Tests **always create a child container** — never resolve from the root container.

---

## Database Drivers

- `DrizzleClient` — the query client.
- `DrizzleDatabaseDriver` — the environment wrapper exposing `db`, `unitOfWorkFactory`, `reset()`, `runMigrations()`, `readMigrations()`, `close()`.
- Production runtime uses `NodePgDriver`.
- Integration tests use `PGliteDriver`.

---

## Channel Projection Ownership (Go-specific)

Cross-service detail layered on top of the general "Read-Model Architecture" section above.

The `channel.*` tables (`channel.channels`, `channel.remotes`, `channel.remote_memberships`, `channel.messages`) are **owned by the Go channel backend**. Go creates them via its own migrations (inside the `channel` Postgres schema, set from `cfg.ServiceName`) and is the only writer. The TS backend mirrors them read-only through Drizzle schemas at `packages/api/src/shared/db/drizzle/schema/channel.ts`.

**TS must never write to `channel.*` tables.** Enforced by convention and by the schema drift test (`packages/api/src/ui/usecases/channel/channel-schema-drift.test.ts`), which fails when Go migrations change columns that the TS Drizzle schema hasn't yet reflected.

The Go layout mirrors the TS folder shape one-for-one:

| Layer | Go folder | TS folder |
|---|---|---|
| Entity | `internal/<ctx>/entities/` | `<ctx>/entities/` |
| Projection record | `internal/<ctx>/projections/` | `<ctx>/projections/<Name>.ts` |
| Aggregate repository | `internal/<ctx>/repositories/<x>/` | `<ctx>/repositories/` |
| Projection repository | `internal/<ctx>/repositories/<x>/<x>_projection_repository.go` | `<ctx>/projections/<Name>ProjectionRepository.ts` |
| Projector | `internal/<ctx>/projections/projectors/*_projector.go` | `<ctx>/projections/projectors/<Name>Projector.ts` |

The Go service additionally has an **anti-corruption layer** in `channel/services/gateway/whatsapp/bootstrap.go` that performs diff-and-emit on WhatsApp sync callbacks — turning bulk reconciliation into per-row events only when something actually changed. This is the "ACL writes directly to the ProjectionRepository" path described under archetypes A / B1 in the Read-Model Architecture section.

> Full applied case: `.specs/2026-04-17-aggregate-projection-architecture.md`.

---

## SDK Generation

Both backends emit OpenAPI 3.1; the SDK is regenerated from those specs:

- **TS api** — `packages/api/public/docs/openapi.json` (served live on port 3030 via the OpenAPI controller).
- **Go channel** — `packages/channel/public/docs/openapi.json` (via `bun x nx run channel:emit-openapi`).

Pipeline: emit OpenAPI → Kubb → `pluginZodRefinements` (in-process post-processor). No pre/post-patches.

Spec contract conventions:

- Enums emitted as `$ref` components (so generated Zod schemas reuse the enum definition).
- Single-value discriminators emitted as `const`.
- `z.unknown()` fields tagged with `x-unknown: true`.
- Cross-field validations carried as `x-zod-refinements` on the **schema that owns the validated fields** (typically the request body), not on the operation.
- Discriminated unions as `oneOf + discriminator + mapping`.

After changing controllers/routes: `bun sdk`. After changing TanStack Router routes: `cd packages/app && bun tsr generate`.

---

## Testing Quick Reference

Source of truth: `.claude/skills/test/SKILL.md`.

| Kind | Location | Mode | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit (Entity / Projection) | `packages/api/src/**/{Entity,Projection}.test.ts` | none | Direct instantiation, no `TestBed`. Projection unit tests cover `applyX` methods. |
| Repository / ProjectionRepository | `packages/api/src/**/Drizzle*Repository.test.ts` | `integration` | Test save/findByKey/delete + complex queries + atomic ops + concurrency |
| Use case / handler | colocated `*.test.ts` | `integration` | Given/When/Then via given helpers |
| Projector | colocated `<Name>Projector.test.ts` | `integration` | Feed each event in `projector.events`, assert projection table row state |
| Flow | `packages/api/tests/flows/` | `mock` | `testBed.pipe(...).run()` |
| Channel projection (Go-owned) | colocated in `ui/usecases/channel/` | `integration` | **Seed projection tables directly via `givenChannel*` helpers**; Go projectors do not run in TS tests. `channel-schema-drift.test.ts` detects Go↔TS migration mismatches |

Given helpers (`packages/api/tests/support/given/`) compose entities by calling repositories directly — they **never** use use cases. Helpers nest: e.g. `givenAppointment` → `givenClinicWithOwner` → `givenUserWithAccount` → `givenUser` + `givenAccount`.

Lifecycle (non-unit tests):
```ts
beforeAll(async () => {
  testContainer = container.createChildContainer()
  testBed = await TestBed.create('integration', { testContainer, ownerId: 'integration-tenant' })
})
beforeEach(async () => { await testBed.reset() })
afterAll(async () => { await testBed.destroy() })
```

Use case tests **do not** repeat `VALIDATION_ERROR` cases — entity tests cover those.

import * as controllers from './controllers'
import * as internalHandlers from './handlers/internal'
import * as externalHandlers from './handlers/external'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY } from './registry'

const ctx = await BoundedContext.create({
	name: 'sales',
	controllers,
	projectors: {},
	internalHandlers,
	externalHandlers,
	registry: INSTANCE_REGISTRY,
})

export default ctx.router

import './errors' // side-effect: register error codes
import type { InstanceRegistry } from '@bk-dash/core-typescript'
import { OrderOverrideRepository } from './repositories/OrderOverrideRepository/OrderOverrideRepository'
import { MockOrderOverrideRepository } from './repositories/OrderOverrideRepository/MockOrderOverrideRepository'
import { DrizzleOrderOverrideRepository } from './repositories/OrderOverrideRepository/DrizzleOrderOverrideRepository'
import { SalesOrderSamplingService } from './services/SalesOrderSamplingService'
import { OrderSamplingService } from '../tenancy/services/OrderSamplingService'
import { OrderQueryService, MockOrderQueryService, DrizzleOrderQueryService } from './services/OrderQueryService'

export const INSTANCE_REGISTRY: InstanceRegistry = {
	mock: [
		{ token: OrderOverrideRepository, instance: MockOrderOverrideRepository },
		{ token: OrderQueryService, instance: MockOrderQueryService },
	],
	integration: [
		{ token: OrderOverrideRepository, instance: DrizzleOrderOverrideRepository },
		// Overrides tenancy's MockOrderSamplingService via load order
		// (tenancy registers first; sales's later entry wins).
		{ token: OrderSamplingService, instance: SalesOrderSamplingService },
		{ token: OrderQueryService, instance: DrizzleOrderQueryService },
	],
	real: [
		{ token: OrderOverrideRepository, instance: DrizzleOrderOverrideRepository },
		{ token: OrderSamplingService, instance: SalesOrderSamplingService },
		{ token: OrderQueryService, instance: DrizzleOrderQueryService },
	],
}

import {
	type InstanceRegistry,
	PGliteDriver,
	NodePgDriver,
	DrizzleDatabaseDriver,
	DrizzleClient,
	UnitOfWorkFactory,
	DomainEventRepository,
	DrizzleDomainEventRepository,
	InternalMediator,
	ExternalMediator,
	EventEmitter2Mediator,
	MockExternalMediator,
	OutboxDispatcher,
	DrizzleOutboxDispatcher,
	MockOutboxDispatcher,
	LoggingService,
	MockLoggingService,
	MailSender,
	ConsoleMailSender,
	Config,
} from '@bk-dash/core-typescript'
import * as schema from '@bk-dash/contracts/db'
import { migrationsDir } from '@bk-dash/contracts/db/migrations'
import { Client } from '@bk-dash/client-typescript'
import type { RequestConfig, ResponseConfig } from '@bk-dash/client-typescript/http'

/**
 * Test request stub for the SDK `Client`. The generated operations call
 * `client(config)` and expect a `{ data, status, statusText }` envelope;
 * for hermetic mock/integration tests we short-circuit with an empty 204
 * so cross-service calls never touch the network. Real mode uses the
 * default ky transport via the configured base URLs.
 */
const stubRequest = async <TData>(_config: RequestConfig): Promise<ResponseConfig<TData>> => ({
	data: undefined as TData,
	status: 204,
	statusText: 'No Content',
})

function mockSdkClient(): Client {
	const fetchStub = stubRequest as unknown as typeof fetch
	return Client.create({
		go: { baseUrl: 'http://stub.local', fetch: fetchStub },
		typescript: { baseUrl: 'http://stub.local', fetch: fetchStub },
	})
}

function realSdkClient(): Client {
	return Client.create({
		go: { baseUrl: Config.env.GO_WORKER_BASE_URL },
		typescript: { baseUrl: Config.env.API_URL },
	})
}

// `Client` has a private constructor (built via `Client.create`), so the class
// object isn't directly assignable to RegistryToken's `abstract new (...)`.
// The runtime reference is still the DI key use cases resolve by type, so cast
// it to a usable token shape — same object, satisfies the registry typing.
const ClientToken = Client as unknown as abstract new (...args: any[]) => Client

import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as authRegistry } from '@auth/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as identityRegistry } from '@identity/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as tenancyRegistry } from '@tenancy/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as billingRegistry } from '@billing/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as integrationRegistry } from '../integration/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as salesRegistry } from '@sales/registry'

import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as analyticsRegistry } from '../analytics/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as financeRegistry } from '../finance/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as catalogRegistry } from '../catalog/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as marketingRegistry } from '../marketing/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as notificationsRegistry } from '@notifications/registry'
import { INSTANCE_REGISTRY as uiRegistry } from '@ui/registry'

const CORE_ENTRIES_MOCK: InstanceRegistry['mock'] = [
	{ token: DrizzleDatabaseDriver, useFactory: () => new PGliteDriver({ schema, migrationsDir }) },
	{ token: DrizzleClient, useFactory: c => (c.resolve(DrizzleDatabaseDriver as any) as any).db },
	{ token: UnitOfWorkFactory, useFactory: c => (c.resolve(DrizzleDatabaseDriver as any) as any).unitOfWorkFactory },
	{ token: InternalMediator, instance: EventEmitter2Mediator },
	{ token: ExternalMediator, instance: MockExternalMediator },
	{ token: OutboxDispatcher, instance: MockOutboxDispatcher },
	{ token: LoggingService, instance: MockLoggingService },
	{ token: MailSender, instance: ConsoleMailSender },
	{ token: ClientToken, useFactory: () => mockSdkClient() },
]

const CORE_ENTRIES_INTEGRATION: InstanceRegistry['integration'] = [
	{ token: DrizzleDatabaseDriver, useFactory: () => new PGliteDriver({ schema, migrationsDir }) },
	{ token: DrizzleClient, useFactory: c => (c.resolve(DrizzleDatabaseDriver as any) as any).db },
	{ token: UnitOfWorkFactory, useFactory: c => (c.resolve(DrizzleDatabaseDriver as any) as any).unitOfWorkFactory },
	{ token: DomainEventRepository, instance: DrizzleDomainEventRepository },
	{ token: InternalMediator, instance: EventEmitter2Mediator },
	{ token: ExternalMediator, instance: EventEmitter2Mediator },
	{ token: OutboxDispatcher, instance: DrizzleOutboxDispatcher },
	{ token: LoggingService, instance: MockLoggingService },
	{ token: MailSender, instance: ConsoleMailSender },
	{ token: ClientToken, useFactory: () => mockSdkClient() },
]

const CORE_ENTRIES_REAL: InstanceRegistry['real'] = [
	{ token: DrizzleDatabaseDriver, useFactory: () => new NodePgDriver({ connectionString: Config.env.DATABASE_URL, schema }) },
	{ token: DrizzleClient, useFactory: c => (c.resolve(DrizzleDatabaseDriver as any) as any).db },
	{ token: UnitOfWorkFactory, useFactory: c => (c.resolve(DrizzleDatabaseDriver as any) as any).unitOfWorkFactory },
	{ token: DomainEventRepository, instance: DrizzleDomainEventRepository },
	{ token: InternalMediator, instance: EventEmitter2Mediator },
	{ token: ExternalMediator, instance: EventEmitter2Mediator },
	{ token: OutboxDispatcher, instance: DrizzleOutboxDispatcher },
	{ token: LoggingService, instance: MockLoggingService },
	{ token: MailSender, instance: ConsoleMailSender },
	{ token: ClientToken, useFactory: () => realSdkClient() },
]

export const ALL_REGISTRIES: InstanceRegistry = {
	mock: [
		...CORE_ENTRIES_MOCK,
		...authRegistry.mock,
		...identityRegistry.mock,
		...tenancyRegistry.mock,
		...billingRegistry.mock,

import { BaseError } from './BaseError'

export type HttpMethod = 'get' | 'post' | 'put' | 'patch' | 'delete' | 'head' | 'ws' | 'sse'

export type HttpClient = Record<HttpMethod, (request: Request) => Promise<Response>>

export type HttpBaseRequest<T = unknown> = T & {
	url: string
	ctx: Record<string, unknown>
	body?: Record<string, unknown>
	headers?: Record<string, string | undefined>
	params?: Record<string, string | undefined>
	query?: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>
	cookie?: Record<string, HttpCookie>
	rawRequest?: Request
}

export type HttpControllerRequest<T> = HttpBaseRequest<T> & {
	raw: Request
}

export class HttpControllerError extends BaseError<string> {
	constructor(
		name: string,
		readonly status: HttpStatusCode,
		message?: string,
	) {
		super(name, message)
	}
}

export interface HttpCookie {
	value: string
	Expires?: Date
	'Max-Age'?: number
	Domain?: string
	Path?: string
	Secure?: boolean
	HttpOnly?: boolean
	SameSite?: 'none' | 'lax' | 'strict'
	Priority?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'
}

export interface HttpBaseResponse<T> {
	status?: HttpStatusCode
	data?: T

file.content:
# Claude Code Configuration — bk-dash

## Project Overview

bk-dash is a polyglot fullstack platform built across **TypeScript + Bun** and **Go**, with three frontends — **React web (TanStack Start + Vite)**, **Astro 5 landing/blog**, **React Native + Expo** — backed by a **single Postgres** with **Drizzle migrations** and **TypeSpec-sourced contracts** generating cross-language SDKs.

Domain: **e-commerce platform** (catalog, sales, marketing, analytics — all externals stubbed for offline use).

## Workspaces

| Path | Stack | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/contracts` | TypeSpec + Drizzle | Source of truth: cross-boundary enums, integration events, DB schema |
| `packages/contracts/generated/{ts,go}` | codegen output | Per-language wire bindings consumed by services |
| `packages/api/typescript` | Bun + Drizzle + tsyringe | Auth, reads, projections, BFF queries |
| `packages/api/go` | Go + sqlc + fx + net/http | Workers, indexers, schedulers |
| `packages/app/react` | React + Vite + TanStack Router/Start | App (`/app/...`) — auth, dashboards, mutations |
| `packages/app/astro` | Astro 5 + MDX + Tailwind 4 | Landing pages + blog + SEO (served at `/`, with locale prefixes) |
| `packages/app/expo` | React Native + Expo Router + Uniwind | Native mobile (iOS + Android) |
| `packages/app/styles` | CSS (design tokens) | Shared tokens consumed by `app-react` + `app-astro` (`@bk-dash/app-styles/tokens.css`). Expo keeps its own `global.css` (uniwind) for now. |
| `packages/client/{ts,go}` | Kubb / oapi-codegen | Symmetric SDKs (each consumes all 2 backends) |
| `packages/e2e` | Playwright | Cross-stack E2E |

Build orchestrated by **Nx** for TS targets + **Go modules** for Go.

A arquitetura é **DDD + Clean Architecture + CQRS + Event-Driven**. Todas as regras existem para manter bounded contexts independentes e o sistema evoluir sem reescritas.

> Profundidade arquitetural por lado: **`docs/BACKEND.md`** e **`docs/FRONTEND.md`**. Sempre leia o doc do lado que você está tocando antes de escrever ou revisar código.

---

## Environment Setup

Pré-requisitos: `bun >= 1.0`, `docker`, `go` (para o channel).

```bash
# 1. Variáveis de ambiente — único arquivo na raiz, lido pelos 3 workspaces (api/channel/app).
cp .env.example .env
# Preencher: JWT_SECRET, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, OPENAI_API_KEY, CHANNEL_GLOBAL_API_KEY

# 2. Pacotes (workspaces Bun)
bun install

# 3. Infra local em Docker (postgres + redis + lgtm para traces/logs/metrics)
bun docker:compose

# 4. Migrações: channel (golang-migrate) + api (drizzle) na ordem certa
bun migrate:dev

# 5. SDK — precisa rodar uma vez antes do app compilar
bun sdk

# 6. Tudo em paralelo (api-ts:3030 + api-go:3032 + app-react:5173 + app-astro:4321)
bun dev
```

Notas:
- O `.env` na raiz é a **única** fonte de verdade. Não há `.env` por workspace.
- Apenas `VITE_*` chegam ao browser.
- Para testes TS, o banco roda em-processo (PGlite). Docker só é necessário para `bun dev` e para o smoke cross-stack.
- LGTM (Grafana 3000, Loki 3100, Tempo 3200, Mimir 9009) recebe traces dos três backends via OTLP (4317/4318).

---

## Commands

```bash
# Desenvolvimento
bun dev                  # api-ts + api-go + app-react + app-astro em paralelo
bun dev:api              # somente os 2 backends
bun dev:api:typescript   # api-ts only
bun dev:api:go           # api-go only
bun dev:app:react        # app-react only (TanStack Start, served under /app)
bun dev:app:astro        # app-astro only (landing + blog, served at /)
bun dev:app:expo         # app-expo only (Expo dev server)

# Build / qualidade
bun run build        # task graph completo (cacheado)
bun tsc              # type-check de todos os workspaces TS
bun run test         # todos os testes (exceto e2e)
bun lint             # lint em todos os workspaces

# SDK + OpenAPI
bun sdk              # regenera SDK (client:build + emit-openapi upstream)
bun emit-openapi     # regenera só os openapi.json (api + channel)

# Banco de dados
bun migrate:dev              # aplica channel (Go) + api (TS) na ordem
bun migrate:create           # gera nova migração Drizzle (api)
bun migrate:channel          # aplica golang-migrate (channel)
bun migrate:channel:down     # reverte última migração channel
bun migrate:channel:create   # cria SQL up/down (channel)

# E2E (Playwright sobe os dev servers via webServer)
bun e2e
bun test:e2e:headed
bun test:e2e:cleanup         # drop de DBs de teste residuais

# Review automatizado
bun review                   # revisa arquivos alterados no git diff
bun review:all               # revisa todo o repo

# Nx direto (quando os scripts de raiz não cobrem)
bun x nx graph
bun x nx run <project>:<target>
bun x nx run-many -t <target>
bun x nx affected -t tsc lint test build --base=dev
bun x nx reset               # limpa cache local
```

---

## Frontend scaffolding

The frontend has a unified scaffolder at `bun cli` (entry: `scripts/cli.ts`, frontend code in `scripts/cli/frontend/`). It's the **first thing to reach for** when creating a route, component, dialog, form, onboarding step, translation key, or input mask. Skills' `scaffold:` lines are the canonical invocations.

Full reference: **`docs/CLI.md`**.

**House rule — "if you wrote it, the CLI should write it":** if during a task you hand-write a shape that would have benefited from a CLI flag, recipe, or new artifact (i.e. you found yourself replicating boilerplate the CLI doesn't yet cover), open a ticket and add it to the CLI before the PR that introduces the hand-written code lands. The CLI exists so that the *next* engineer doesn't re-discover the same shape. If extending the CLI before shipping the feature would block the feature, file the gap as a follow-up issue, link it from the PR, and resolve it within one week.

The CLI is a **scaffolder**, not a code generator — `tsc` errors immediately after generation are expected (missing imports, unknown SDK identifiers). The agent wires them up. See `docs/CLI.md` §1 for the philosophy.

---

## First-Class Citizens

A composição do código é sempre a mesma — em cada contexto e em cada feature. Esta lista decide **onde** o problema de negócio cabe. Foco no **propósito de negócio**; detalhes técnicos vivem em `docs/BACKEND.md` / `docs/FRONTEND.md`.

### Backend

**BoundedContext** — uma fatia de negócio (`patient`, `appointment`, `clinic`, `doctor`...). Tudo que se refere a essa área vive numa pasta com o mesmo formato. Modelando uma área nova (ex.: `billing`) → cria um novo bounded context.

**Entity / AggregateRoot** — a "coisa" do negócio com identidade e regras: `Patient`, `Appointment`, `Clinic`. É a entidade que decide se uma mudança é válida (status, atribuições, datas). Onde moram as invariantes do tipo *"um agendamento não pode ser confirmado depois de cancelado"*. **Levanta domain events** quando algo importante acontece.

**Value Object** — um conceito definido pelo valor, sem identidade: `CPF`, `Email`, `Money`, `DateRange`. Auto-validado: um CPF inválido não existe. Vive dentro de entidades.

**Enum** — lista fechada de estados: `AppointmentStatus`, `DayOfWeek`, `PaymentType`. Quando o negócio diz "isso só pode ser A, B ou C", você codifica como enum. Sempre pareado com `pgEnum` no banco.

**Schema (Zod)** — a forma de qualquer dado em runtime. Schemas não são um detalhe de controller — são o vocabulário estrutural compartilhado por todo lugar que precisa validar entrada, descrever um payload ou inferir um tipo:

- **Entities** descrevem sua própria forma com Zod (`AppointmentSchema`); o `.create()` valida primitivos contra esse schema antes de construir a instância. A migração do banco é **derivada** desse schema, não o contrário.
- **Value Objects** validam o valor de entrada (`CPFSchema`, `EmailSchema`) — um VO inválido nunca chega a existir.
- **Use cases** declaram `InputSchema` (primitivos) e `OutputSchema` que viram o contrato chamável.
- **Controllers** declaram schemas expressivos (regex, `.refine()`, cross-field) — são esses que viram a SDK via OpenAPI.
- **Domain events** e **integration events** carregam payload tipado por `z.domainEvent({...})` / `z.integrationEvent({...})`.
- **Forms no frontend** consomem o **mesmo** schema que o controller — uma fonte de verdade, validação simétrica.

Heurística: precisa validar entrada ou definir estrutura em runtime? **Escreva um schema.** Schemas duplicados entre camadas são bandeira vermelha — extraia para `shared/` ou componha (`.and()`, `.pick()`, `.extend()` quando legítimo) em vez de redigitar.

**Error (Domain / Application)** — o vocabulário do que pode dar errado no negócio. **Toda invariante violável é um erro nomeado**, não uma string solta nem um `throw new Error("...")`.

- **DomainErrors** — invariantes de negócio: `APPOINTMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED`, `INSUFFICIENT_STOCK`, `INVALID_CPF`, `DOCTOR_NOT_AVAILABLE_AT_TIME`. Levantados **por entidades e value objects** quando algo viola uma regra do domínio. Se você está escrevendo um método em `Appointment` e precisa dizer "isso não pode acontecer porque...", você está descobrindo um `DomainError`.
- **ApplicationErrors** — condições da camada de aplicação: `PATIENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ALREADY_EXISTS`, `UNAUTHORIZED`. Levantados **por use cases e handlers** ao orquestrar (lookup falhou, recurso ausente, autorização inválida).

Cada erro carrega código + status HTTP + chave i18n — mapeados centralmente no `GlobalErrorMapper`. O frontend recebe o código e exibe a tradução; o teste assertiva no código, nunca na mensagem. Quem dispara: `throw new BaseError<DomainErrors>('APPOINTMENT_ALREADY_CONFIRMED')`.

> Erros são a fronteira entre "regra de negócio" e "comportamento do sistema". Se você se pegou validando algo num controller que poderia ser uma invariante, esse algo provavelmente quer virar um `DomainError` levantado pela entidade.

**Use Case (command)** — **uma operação de negócio**: `CreateAppointment`, `ConfirmAppointment`, `CancelSubscription`. **Um por intenção.** É chamado pelo controller, que é disparado pelo frontend quando o usuário clica num botão. Orquestra: carrega entidades via repositórios, chama métodos nelas, salva, persiste eventos. Tudo dentro de um `UnitOfWork` (transação). **Se você precisa modelar algo de negócio, é aqui que vai parar.**

**Query Use Case** — leitura específica para uma tela. Vive no contexto `ui` (BFF pattern). Não passa por entidades — fala direto com Drizzle para montar o DTO que a UI quer. Perfeito para listagens, dashboards, detalhes.

**Controller** — a porta HTTP. Recebe o request, valida com Zod, chama um use case, devolve a resposta. **Não pensa.** Nunca toca repositório.

**Repository** — a ponte entre entidade e banco. `findById`, `save`, `delete`, mais buscas por identificador (`findByEmail`, `findByCpf`). Devolve entidade rehidratada, recebe entidade para salvar.

**Service** — lógica que não cabe em uma entidade (cálculos cross-entity, integrações externas, regras transversais). Use cases compõem services + entidades.

**Domain Event** — fato passado dentro de **um** bounded context: `AppointmentConfirmed`, `PatientRegistered`. A entidade levanta; o handler interno reage. **Não cruza serviço.**

**Integration Event** — fato que cruza contextos ou serviços (Go ↔ TS): `shared.appointmentConfirmed` é ouvido pelo channel para mandar a confirmação por WhatsApp. **Publicado somente por handlers**, nunca por use cases.

**Handler (internal / external)** — onde os side-effects do **write-side** vivem.
- `internal.ts` reage a domain events do **próprio** contexto. Pode publicar um integration event para outros, ou disparar outro use case interno.
- `external.ts` reage a integration events vindos de outros contextos/serviços.
- Padrão típico: *"quando um paciente se registra, mande email de boas-vindas e crie a primeira sessão"*.

**Projection** — o "espelho de leitura" de uma área. Uma tabela materializada otimizada para uma view específica (ex.: `channel_messages`, `channel_remotes`, `MonthlyStats`). **Free record, sem base class** — classe simples com `constructor(public props: <Name>ProjectionProps)`. Schema Zod flat define a forma; **sem invariantes**, sem regras de negócio. A Projection é a **fonte de verdade** do que muda nela:
- Exporta `type <Name>ProjectionEvent = A | B | C` — union de todos os eventos que afetam ela. O Projector importa esse tipo como generic.
- **Criação (`static create(event)`)** — **método overloaded** — uma signature por evento que pode criar a row (ex.: `static create(event: MessageReceivedEvent)`, `static create(event: MessageSentEvent)`), uma implementação que faz `switch (event.name)` e constrói via `new MessageProjection({...})`. Type system enforça "só esses eventos podem me criar".
- **Mutação (`applyEvent(event)`)** — **método overloaded** — uma signature por evento que muta state (ex.: `applyEvent(event: MessageEditedEvent)`, `applyEvent(event: MessageDeletedEvent)`), uma implementação com `switch (event.name)` mutando `this.props`. Caminho canônico: `find → applyEvent → save`.
- **Sem método pra eventos atômicos** (`markDeliveredMany`, `incrementUnreadCount`) — esses são edge cases que vivem direto no repo, justificados por hot row / bulk / monotonic / conditional / cache-mirror.

Vive em `<ctx>/projections/<Name>.ts`. Existe quando o read-model é diferente do write-model (denormalização, agregação, cache cross-contexto). **Cross-aggregate cross-context** (read shape que spans contextos) vive em `ui/projections/`, não nos contextos de origem.

**ProjectionRepository** — o vocabulário **atômico** para escrever na projection: `insertIfNew`, `upsertMany`, `incrementUnreadCount`, `markDeliveredMany`, `setIfGreater*`. É aqui que a atomicidade mora — em vez de `find → mutate → save` (que causa N+1 e race), Projectors chamam ops atômicas que o banco resolve num único `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`. Sem base interface — cada repo declara as ops que precisa, igual ao Repository do write-side.

**Projector** — o **handler do read-side**. Uma classe por Projection, escuta múltiplos eventos. Diferente do Handler (write-side effects ou publica integration events), o Projector **só** escreve em projeções via sua `ProjectionRepository`. **Async via outbox por default**, **inline opcional** dentro de um use case quando precisa de read-after-write na mesma request. Vive em `<ctx>/projections/projectors/<Name>Projector.ts`. Shape:
- A generic vem **da Projection**: `extends Projector<MessageProjectionEvent>`. O Projector não declara união local.
- Implementa `handle(event, tx?)` com um **plain `switch (event.name)`**. Discriminated-union narrowing por `case`, exhaustiveness via `default: const _: never = event`. **Sem mapped types, sem record, sem magia TS.** Declara `events: readonly string[]` listando os nomes registrados.
- **Caminho canônico para mutação: `find → projection.applyEvent(event) → save`.** A Projection é dona da lógica de transição; o repo só precisa de `findByKey` + `save` + `insertIfNew` pra atender o canon.
- **Criação**: `repo.insertIfNew(MessageProjection.create(event), tx)` — `MessageProjection.create` é overloaded e escolhe a branch certa pelo `event.name`.
- **Atomic ops são edge cases**. Adiciona um método atômico ao repo só quando algum trigger justifica: hot row contention, bulk over N rows, monotonic constraint (set-if-greater), conditional update, ou cache-mirror upsert. Caso contrário, segue no `find → applyEvent → save`.

**Middleware** — cross-cutting de HTTP (auth, tenant, logging). Defaults por contexto, override por controller.

**UnitOfWork / Outbox / Mediators** — infra de evento: a transação que salva entidade + evento atomicamente, o despachante que lê o outbox e dispara o handler, o mediator que entrega o evento. O detalhe está em `docs/BACKEND.md` ("Event Architecture").

### Frontend

**Route** — uma URL (ex.: `/clinics/$clinicId/patients`). É uma **casca fina**: define o contrato da URL (path, search params, breadcrumb, errorComponent), monta o layout e decide **quais** componentes aparecem. **Não busca dado para passar pra baixo.**

**Component** — vive em `-components/` da route. Cada componente **dona seus próprios dados**: lê search params via `routeApi.useSearch()`, lê estado de cliente via Zustand, dispara queries/mutations SDK por si só. Sem prop-drilling de dado, search ou callback. Quando precisa do estado "carregando", renderiza skeleton inline; UI estática permanece visível enquanto os dados chegam.
- Componentes "container" (que orquestram uma seção da tela) usam o **sufixo `Section`** apenas como convenção de nome (`PatientListSection`) — vivem em `-components/` como qualquer outro. Não é uma pasta separada nem uma camada extra.
- Componentes folha (renderizados N vezes num `.map()`: cards, rows, badges) **recebem o item por prop** — o pai dono da lista mapeia.

**Primitive** (`@/components/ui/*`) — átomo de design system (Button, Card, Dialog) sobre Base UI + CVA.

**Form** — TanStack Form + schema da SDK. Mesmo Zod que o backend valida — zero sincronização manual.

**Store (Zustand)** — estado interativo do cliente que não cabe em URL (IDs selecionados compartilhados entre componentes, toggles de UI, dialog aberto). Para persistir entre refreshes, use `persist`.

**Hook** — helper transversal (`useDebouncedSearch`, `useDialogStore`, `useSession`).

### Como eles se ligam — fluxo de exemplo

> Usuário clica "Confirmar agendamento" no app:

1. **Component** (ex.: `AppointmentCardSection`) chama `useConfirmAppointment()` (mutation gerada pela SDK).
2. SDK bate em **Controller** `POST /appointments/:id/confirm`.
3. Controller valida com **Schema** Zod e chama **Use Case** `ConfirmAppointment`.
4. Use case carrega `Appointment` via **Repository**, chama `appointment.confirm()` (regra na **Entity**).
5. Entity valida invariante, muda status (**Enum** `AppointmentStatus`), levanta **Domain Event** `AppointmentConfirmed`.
6. Use case salva entidade + evento na **mesma transação** (UnitOfWork → outbox).
7. **OutboxDispatcher** lê o outbox e entrega o evento ao `InternalMediator`, que faz fan-out para **todos** os assinantes registrados naquele evento:
   - **Handler interno** do contexto `appointment` publica **Integration Event** `shared.appointmentConfirmed` no Kafka.
   - **Projector** `PatientProjector` (mora em `patient/projections/projectors/`, escuta `AppointmentConfirmed` para advancing o `nextAppointmentAt` na `PatientProjection`) chama `patientProjectionRepo.setIfGreaterNextAppointment(...)` — op atômica, sem find.
8. **Channel (Go)** consome o integration event do Kafka, e seu `external.ts` handler dispara um use case interno que manda a notificação por WhatsApp.
9. No `channel`, quando a notificação volta como `MessageSent`, o `MessageProjector` (Go) insere a linha em `channel_messages` via `repo.insertIfNew(...)` — outra op atômica.

Cada citizen tem **uma responsabilidade** no fluxo: entity decide se a mudança é válida, use case orquestra a transação, handler propaga side-effects no write-side, projector atualiza read-models, integration event atravessa contextos/serviços. Nenhum deles sabe sobre os outros diretamente — todos se conhecem por eventos.

## SDK — o tendão entre backend e frontend

A SDK não é "um cliente HTTP". Ela é **o contrato compartilhado** que permite backend e frontend serem desenvolvidos em paralelo sem se atropelarem.

```
Controller (Zod schema)
    └─► api emite openapi.json
            └─► Kubb gera hooks + schemas + tipos + query keys
                    └─► app importa de '@bk-dash/monorepo-sdk/app'
```

**O que a SDK exporta para o frontend:**

- Hooks React Query (`useListPatients`, `useCreateAppointment`, `useConfirmAppointment`).
- Schemas Zod prontos para `validators` do TanStack Form.
- Tipos TS para `defaultValues`, props, etc.
- Enums (`AppointmentStatus`) — mesma fonte que o banco.
- Query keys para `invalidateQueries`.

**Por que isso destrava trabalho paralelo:**

1. Backend modela controller + schema → roda `bun sdk`.
2. Frontend já tem hook tipado para chamar — mesmo antes do use case existir, dá pra trabalhar contra um mock.
3. Mudou o schema do backend? `bun sdk` e o `tsc` do app reclama nos pontos exatos que precisam adaptar.

**Regras duras:**

- Frontend **só** consome dados do backend pela SDK. Nunca `fetch` direto.
- Dentro do `api`, **nunca** use o cliente HTTP da SDK (cria ciclo). Para ler outro contexto: importe o `Repository` dele.
- Sempre rode `bun sdk` depois de mexer em controller/schema.
- Rode `cd packages/app && bun tsr generate` depois de criar/mover rota.

> Convenções OpenAPI (enums como `$ref`, `x-zod-refinements`, discriminadores `const`) e a pipeline Kubb estão em `docs/BACKEND.md`.

## Testing — TDD, Red/Green, Given, Sandbox

Tests are first-class. Substituem boa parte da "documentação viva" da arquitetura.

### Ciclo Red / Green / Refactor

1. **Red** — escreva o teste do comportamento que ainda não existe (entity, use case, handler). Deve falhar com erro útil.
2. **Green** — implementação mínima para passar.
3. **Refactor** — colha os testes como rede de segurança.

### As 4 camadas de teste

| Tipo | Onde | Modo DI | Quando usar |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Unit** | `src/**/Entity.test.ts` | nenhum (instanciação direta) | Invariantes de entidades / value objects |
| **Repository** | `src/**/Drizzle*Repository.test.ts` | `integration` | `save / findById / delete` + queries complexas |
| **Use case / Handler** | colocado `*.test.ts` | `integration` | Comportamento end-to-end de uma operação |
| **Flow** | `packages/api/tests/flows/` | `mock` | Coreografias entre use cases (sagas) |

### Sandbox: banco em-processo

Testes não dependem de Docker. O `DrizzleDatabaseDriver` no modo `integration` usa **PGlite** — Postgres rodando dentro do processo. `reset()` zera o estado entre testes, e as mesmas migrations da produção são aplicadas — então o que passa no teste passa no Postgres real.

```ts
beforeAll(async () => {
  testContainer = container.createChildContainer()      // DI isolada por suite
  testBed = await TestBed.create('integration', {
    testContainer,
    ownerId: 'integration-tenant',
  })
})
beforeEach(async () => { await testBed.reset() })       // estado limpo por teste
afterAll(async () => { await testBed.destroy() })
```

### Interfaces e DI por ambiente

Cada contexto exporta um `registry.ts` com bindings para três ambientes:

- `mock` — `MockUnitOfWorkFactory`, `MockOutboxDispatcher`, `OutboxAwareMockDomainEventRepository`, mediators em memória. **Flow tests** usam isso.
- `integration` — driver PGlite + outbox e mediators reais. Testes de repositório, use case e handler usam isso.
- `real` — `NodePgDriver`, `RedisExternalMediator`, `BullMQ`. Produção.

O teste resolve dependências via `child container`. Você troca uma implementação só para a suíte sem afetar o resto.

### Given helpers — montando estado sem use case

Em `packages/api/tests/support/given/` há helpers compostos que criam estado **direto via repositórios** — nunca via use case. Isso garante que um teste de `CancelAppointment` não dependa de `CreateAppointment` estar correto.

```ts
const { appointment, clinic, patient } = await givenAppointment(testBed, {
  // overrides opcionais
})
```

Helpers se aninham: `givenAppointment` → `givenClinicWithOwner` → `givenUserWithAccount` → `givenUser` + `givenAccount`.

### Eventos em teste

No modo `integration`, o outbox e o `OutboxDispatcher` rodam de verdade. Você pode:

- Disparar um use case.
- Esperar o handler reagir.
- Assertar que o evento foi salvo, despachado e o handler tratou.

Para isolar a unidade testada, o `MockExternalMediator` (no modo `mock`) captura integration events sem publicar — útil em flow tests.

### Regra de ouro

Testes de **use case não repetem** os casos de `VALIDATION_ERROR` — esses são cobertos pelos testes de entidade. Use case testa orquestração, não regra de campo.

> Detalhes completos: `.claude/skills/test/SKILL.md`.

## Review

Code review tem dois canais:

**Manual / interativo:** skill `/review` carrega o checklist da `registry.yaml` da skill correspondente ao artefato e devolve uma lista priorizada de bad practices encontrados.

**Em batch (CLI):** `scripts/review.ts` revisa arquivos em paralelo com agentes Claude, usando os registries compilados em checklists compactos.

```bash
bun review                                 # git diff
bun review:all                             # repo inteiro
bun scripts/review.ts --staged             # arquivos staged
bun scripts/review.ts --pr                 # branch atual vs dev
bun scripts/review.ts --backend --context appointment
bun scripts/review.ts --frontend --all
```

Opções úteis: `--parallel N`, `--output dir/`, `--thorough` (Opus em vez de Sonnet), `--no-cascade`.

A saída inclui **análise de cascata**: rastreia imports bottom-up para indicar quais correções resolvem várias violações ao mesmo tempo (`_cascade-analysis.md`).
